For the stone
The body beinge first cleansed by some stomach pills, drinke in the morn=
=inge a large draught of possett drinke made of Ale and white wine, wherein
is mixed 2 or 3 spoonfulls of the Sirrup of Althea, and walke moderately
after it. sometimes adde a spoonfull of the oyle of sweete Almonds new
drawen, and sometime a little Juice of Lemons; If you would some
times have it more diereticall, as when the stone shall paine you in like
Kidneys, Boile in the possett drink a little of the Rootes of Fennell and Parsley
with a spoonfull of theire seedes; If your stomack will endure
Buttermilke, drinke in the morninge a good draught with a little nutmegg
and Sugar, and drinke it often while it is in Breakinge, that is before
it may bee clearly separated from the Butter; sometimes drinke
whey with a spoonfull or two of the Sirrup of Lemons mixed with it
or the Sirrup of Althea; A Conserve of Eringo Roots is good to eate
often at bedtime, or a Conserve of Hepps./.





No For The Syatica or Hipp Gowte

Take one pound of Blacke Soape, Aqya vita one pinte sallett oyle one Gill
Juice of Ruta one Hill, Putt the soape Aqua vitae and Rue into a panne
of brasse and let them boile very gently over a hott fire that is cleare lifte
flameinge, sett your stuffe on fire and when boyled till almost thicke then
putt to it your oyle, sett it over the fire and boile gently till it will leave
the panne side, as doth starch when boyled enough take it and spreade itt
on a lambs skinne on the fleish side, lay it hott to the place of greife as you
can suffer it, lett it lye thereon 3 days, if it fall not off, take itt off, and
renew the plaister layinge it hott on as formerly. this will ease the paine
if it bee within the space of 3 yeares, since it first came: Lay the plaister
from the hipp bone to the knee, twill ease in 3 days space. Probat.

To make the spleene Salve

Take Mellilote, Camomile of each 3 handfulls, Parsley, Plaintaine of each an
handfull, of sweete sheeps suett a pound, of virgins waxe 12 ounces of Rosen
three pound, of white wine a pinte; shredde the waxe and Suett and
beate the Rosen, and sett it over the fire till all bee melted, then take it
off, cover it close, and lett it stand seven dayes in a Cellar, Then sett itt
over the fire againe, and let it boyle halfe an hower, Then take it off and
straine it into dishes, puttinge a litle water into the bottome of the dishes
first, when tis could you may fould it upp close in papers and it will keepe
4 or 5 yeares, Let it bee spreade upon Lambe skinn, and applyed
unto the region of the spleene, it cleanses and Comforts it admirably

Sweete marivrame, Borrage Cowslipp flowers ana man. - the leaves of 12
marigolds: Groats bruised in a morter, with a wodden Pestell 4 spoonfulls

a pottinger full att a time into which beinge hott putt 3 or 4 spoonfull of

with vomitinge

an exselentt Recept for the Stone Ia: Pembroock water
Take 3 handfull of march mallowes, one handfull of Parsley
one handfull of horse Reddish Roots, one handfull of Redd Fennell
but not of the seedes and an handfull of spinage choppe all these
together as small as you can and put them into 8 Pottle full of
milke new from the Cowe to steepe for 24 howers; then distill
it and let the Patient take 7 or 8 spoonfulls of the water
in the morneing fasting for some 3 or 4 dayes before and after
the fall of the moone, and as longe before and after the new of
the moone minglinge with it some 2 or 3 spoonfulls of white
wine or cyder, and a little sugar, and Continuinge to doe this
all the yeare longe, it will (by Gods assistance) soe mollifie
and dissolve the stone, as it will make it come away by degrees
from the party, though hee cannot perceive any greate ease
by it in one present fitt/.

Sir Theodore Mayern's Emulsion which he used to give in
three cases relating to the Stone.

When there is any Sharpness of urine
When the party makes any bloody water
Take 2 Spoonfulls of french Barly & boyle it in two severall waters, then take it
out & put it in two quarts of fresh water with about half an ounce of liquorish
Sliced & towed pretty small, & boyle these till a pint is consum'd that there
remains only three pints. then half an ounce of each of the four cold seeds
& beat then in a Stone Mortar with a little of your boyled water, & squeeze
out the Liquor very hard through a cloth & mix it with your water till it looks
white like milk, & Sweeten it with Syrrup of Althea, & drink of it half a
pint at a time upon an Empty Stomack morning & night, or in ye Evening
The best way to prevent ye prevailing of the Stone & Paine is to take Slippery
things as marsh mallow Roots about half an ounce boiled in chicken broth
or any spoon-meat the party likes, & interchangeably posset ale, wherein
is boyled pellitory of the wall, Sweetened with Syrrop of Althea or only made
of marshmallows, or 2 or 3 Spoonfulls of oyl of Sweet almonds & put
thereto as much Juice of Lemons well Sweetened with white Sugar candy,
& take it upon an Empty Stomack fasting an hour after it. Syrrop of Althea
is good also to be taken a Spoonfull alone at a time. To use these enterchan
geably is very good against ye Stone.





Doctor Edmonds Vomit of Salt preventing of pestilential Distempers.
Take bay salt & burn it in an Iron pan or Shovell till it leaves crackling & is of a
yellowish white, but it must bekept stirring all the while wth some Iron thing
to keep it from running into water for that spoyls it. Then put it into water --
till it makes it tast brackish, then let it stand & settle, & then poure off the
cleare, & give of it to a man or woman a quarter of a pint or 6 ounces --
fasting & to a child 4 or 5 spoonfulls at a time.
For a perfume of Salt in any infectous times.
One pound of white Salt, one pound of Salt peter, one ounce of Amber, Beat
all these together into powder; then heat a shovell & sprinkle of this powder
upon it 3 or 4 times a day, this is good to cure an infectious ayre, and --
to prevent infection.

Take Roots of Angelica, Masterwort, Butter Burre
Piony of each halfe a Pound, Meum or Sprignall, Scorronera

Leaves of Rue, Rosemary, Balme, Carduus Benedictus,

Take of Sage, Salladine, Rosemary, Rue, Rosabolis
Mugwort, Pimpernell, dragons, Scabious, Agrimony
Balme, Scordium, Cardus Benedictus, Betony flowers
and leaves; Centry topps and flowers, St Johns wort
flowers and topps; Meade sweete and flowers, Clove
gilliflowers, of each of these a good handfull.





Then take the Roots of Butterburrs Tormentile. Angelica
Ellicampane, Piony, Gentian, Zeadoary, Snake Roots Liquorice
Rootes, of Contrareum Roots cleane scraped and Thinn sliced
of each of them three quarters of an ounce; Angellica seeds
Citron seedes, Betony seedes of each one ounce; Let the hearbes
bee first washed, and then shake them in a linen cloth till they bee
dry, then shredd the hearbes altogether, and mixinge them with
the Rootes; putt them altogether in a gallon and a halfe of the
best white wine, and lett them all steepe together in a large
earthen Pott well glazed, and soe let them stand covered close
4 dayes or a weeke, stirringe them well each day, then still
altogether in a Limbeck still, keepeing could water in the heade
of the Limbeck, and receive the water into Pinte bottles, till
you finde it begin to runn sower, then you may mingle it to what
strength you thinke fitt; Let your bottle bee cleane washed
and throughly dryed, before you put the water into them
and stoppe them very close, you must paste the still downe
with paste made of Rye meale vinegar and whites of Eggs, least
any of the virtue breath forth, and if the still bee not large you
may devide the quantity into two stills; It is most proper to
bee given if the Party bee sick uppon an empty stomack and may
bee given with Mithridate or Diascordium, Bezar or unicorns
horne or harts horne, very meete in popular or Contagious
Sicknesses, and very proper to bee mingled in Julepps, which
are made to Comfort the stomack and open obstructions

And resiste malignity in contagious or infectious sicknesse
puttinge to a pinte of coolinge julepp 3 or 4 spoonfulls of the
first or second runinge that is the strongest, of the
strongest may bee given to man or woman 4 or 5 spoonfull
of the smaller sorte of all for children that are very young
3 or 4 spoonfull; But bee sure to receive none of the
water when it runns sowre; It may bee given lukewarm
with sirrupp of gilliflowers, or it may bee given could
or by it selfe./

Belgarde's Water for the Stone & Gravell in ye Kidneys.
Take of spirit of wine two pounds, Turbith, mastick, cloves, nutmegs, galin-
gal, cubwebs, wood of Aloes of each half an ounce. Cypress, Turpentine,
English honey, Juniper berry of each four ounces. Distill the aforesaid things
in a glass still wth soft fire, till the ingredients be dry. The liquor cureth ye
gravell, stone, or Ulcer in the kidneys. Take one spoonfull in ye morning
in fair water or small ale.

A Playster for the Worms
Collaquintida an Apple, Savine & centory of each a pugil, Juice of Rue
& wormwood of each 3 spoonfulls, of Aloes & wormseed of each two drams
large mace & saffron powderd of each a dram, half the gall of an ox, and
English honey 3 ounces, of swines grease the quantity of a wallnut, Let
all these be prepared according to Art and wth old beer boyled to the
consistence of a playster & applyed warme.

recipes.raw_title: For the Cough of ye Lunges or consumption
recipes.raw_body:
Take one ounce of China roots sliced small & thin & sett
them to steep one whole night in fountaine water, there being
3 aile quarts of ye water: The next morning powre ye water & the
China into an earthen pott wth a narrow mouth, such as ye Doctors
call diel-potts: Then put into ye pot 3 quarters of an ounce
of English Liquoras cleane scrapd & slitt: also 3 quarters of an ounce
of Anniseeds well cleansd, & halfe a pound of Raisons of ye sunne
well washt, & stoned: this done cover ye pott wth its cover, & set it
to boyle on a gentle charcoale fire untill halfe ye water be
consumd, then take it from ye fire, & let it stand coverd at
most a quarter of an hour, then straine it, & keep it in an
earthen pott for your use.
Every morning drinke a beer glasse full of it warme,
& at meals drink it cold: & when you goe to bed another beere
glasse warme. This drinke must be made fresh euery day
for twenty one daies:  The second day you make this drinke
you must putt one ounce & a halfe of China Roots to steepe:
the 3d day 2 ounces, the 4th day 2 ounces & a halfe, ye 5th day
3 ounces: & soe continue untill one & twenty daies are finishd.
The day before you intend to take this diet drinke you
must purge: the 10th or 12th day purge againe: the 22nd day
or on ye day you leaue it purge againe. If this chance
to bind ye body yt you goe not to stoole in 24 hours, then
leaue out ye Raisons of ye sunne, & put in halfe a pound
of prunes, & when you find your body soluble leaue out
ye prunes, & put in ye Raisons againe, & is to be observed, yt in
ye time you are taking this drinke you are to use noe other.
This diet drinke hath wrought admirable Effects upon
several persons upon my own experience, even to a
miracle.

Take the roots of daffodills newgathered; scrape them & slice
them thine; & fill a small bagg as bigg as 3 fingers let the
bagg bee as bigg silke & hange it about the Childs necke; soe
as it may bee upon the stomacke; use this at the fitts first
cominge & you shall see the abatement

recipes.raw_title: for spitinge of blood
recipes.raw_body:
Make water grewell with Charity choped small, & let it
be your breake fast everie morninge

An Exelent syrup for a stickinge cough

Take A quart of Runninge water; & halfe a handfull of the
topps & leaves of penniroyall; boyle it then to halfe; then let
it run through a cloth with out squeezinge it; & boyle it with
sugar to a syrup drinke it morning & eveninge as hot as you
can indure it

for the ptisick

Take a hanful of bettony & boyle it in 3 pints of new milk
lett it stand all night & the next day drinke it warme
& take of it 3 or 4 dayes

for a stuffinge

Halfe a pint of Hysop water as much whit wine a handfull of
brambbleleaves, put in A litle licoraiss & anniseede briused, boyle
them & put thereto 2 o℥ of hard sugar

To stay vomitinge in any sicknesse

Take the disstilled water of mint of life & drinke it warmed
with a litle sugar & nutmegg, or burne Clalret wine & lett
it bee stronge of the mints

to Rid phlegme

Take 30 leaves of mercary, 60 of sorrell 10 of borage
30 of violats, 30 of mallowes; boyle these in a quart of water
to a pint & make either Almond millke or aposset therewith &
drinke the posset all

for ye bloody fluxe

Take 3 or 4 dropps of ye oyle of Juniper berries in a litle
Cleere wine give the patient as much Diascordium as a nut
megg maide up in pills with a litle sugar when hee goes to bed
if you would stay it sudenly give it in a draught of
sorrell, lichoras or borrage water







The Receipt to make ye myce of Lichorise 36

Take a quarter of A pint & som what more of the iuyce of hysop
then make it up a full halfe pint with the iuyce of cleate
leaves; put to these halfe A pint of hysop water; a quarter of a
pound of Lychoras searced seeth all these together gently
stirringe it continually; till it bee of A resonable thicknesse
then bray it with a spoone throught a linnen streaner, take ye
finest & put it in to a skillet againe with a quarter of a pound
of browne sugar candy & 4 ℥ of lofe sugar beaten, boyle
these Continualy stirringe them till it riseth & leeve from ye
skillets bottom; then take it at; & brayit upon a trencher till it
com to aperfect lycoras colour & almost cold, then dust your
hands with a litle licoras powder & make it up in to cakes;
lay them upon a trencher likewise dusted with licoras powder
& set them to dry; when you use it take a litle peece & soeone
peece after another & lett it dissolve in your mouth; swallowinge
it downe, with the spitle as it dissolveth; you may hold it under
tongue when you are in leed.

A drinke for Aconsumption

Boyle in your wort of laurell of land bettonie of Red sage
of each an hand full a quarter of apound of anniseeds; beat ye
anniseeds & put them in to a bagg; & boyle them all in the ale
when the ale is well boyled; streane out the hearbs & worke
upthe ale as you use to doe with any other ale drinke
hange the bagg with with ye anniseeds at the bunge hole of you
r vessell

for The kinge cough

Take kaine weed & posset boyle it in posset ale, & drinke it
morninge & eveninge som call it help or kindweed

for the whoopinge cough

Take a pippin & cut of the top & core it; then fill it with
mustard seede & lay on the top againe, then rost it verie
tender; & eat it when you goe to bed

another for the same

Take rasins stoned; browne sugar candy & Anniseeds
beat them to gether to a past & eat of it often

recipes.raw_title: An appved medicen for a cough when blood
recipes.raw_body:
is rased
Take A pint of faire water & halfe a handfull of Comfrey roots
sliced & scraped a qrter of a handfull of colts foote leaves a sticke
or 2 of licorise sliced & scraped boyle them together in the water
to halfe a pint; streine it & put to it halfe a pint of English honey
then cleare it put it in to a glasse once in 3 hours, take a spoonfull
night & day
for a cough
Take the pith from dried ashen keyes, beat it to powder; mixe
the powder with as much English hony as will make it a past
make thereof pilles to ake when you ly to sleepe, or at any
other time of the day
Rowles for stuffinge in the stomacke for ye cough of
the lungs; or any other to bee taken like the .... of lichorise
Take a pound of sugar beaten & finly searced, 4℥ of lichoris
serced; halfe an o℥ allcampane roots in powder, halfe an o℥ of
gum dragon; dissolved in hysop water, mingle the powder toge
ther make it into a stiff past, then make it up in rolles or
cakes; keepe it in a box neere the fire, let it dissolve in your
mouth & swallow it downe by litle & litle
for the whoopinge cough
Rost a turnip squice out the iuce, & mingle that with
juce with sugar & take it often; it is good likewise to
bath the soles of the feet, with beere butter & salt when
you goe to bed
A Cleereinge drinke for them that are trobled
with any Cloginge of phlegms in the stomack
Take a pottle of runninge water halfe a handfull of parsley
roots as much of fennell roots halfe a handfull of the tops of
hysop; pith the roots & boyle all these together till halfe
bee wasted; then streine it, & put thereto a qter of a pint
of hony, as much of wine vinegar let them boyle a litle
together; & soe keepe it for your use; drinke of it in the
morninge fastinge & 2 houres before super it will raise much
phleggme phlegme; it is also verie good to gargle it putinge
to 4 spoonfulls thereof halfe a spoon full of mustard
gargle often





A Cullis for a consumption
Take the one halfe of an ould Cocke, get from the butchers a pound
of the Pith out of the back bone of an oxe som motton bones 3
neathers harts washed in wine halfe an ounce of harts horne as
much Ivory; 3 qters of China sliced 2 large nutmeggs quartered
of Canded Lingo roots sliced 5 dates stoned halfe an  of comfrey
roots sliced one hand full of raisins of the son stoned, of bettony,
winter savory Broad time, mariarum,piny royall, & rosemary
of Each a small quantity 2 small parsley roots, a blade or 2 of
Large mace; boyle therein 5 peices of fine gould, a crust of bread
& a small handfull of Redrose leaves; boyle your meat & all your
ingradients before; in a pipkin with 3 pottles of springe water
upon asoft fire; cum it and lett it boyle untill it com to the height
of a culleis, scume of that fatt & pserve it for your use.

For any cough
Take oyle of sweet almonds mingle with browne stone sugar
to allmost a past & deale there of often.

For A cough or stuffinge
mix 2 ounces of syrup of red popiys with 4  of Hisop
water take 2 spoon fulls at atime, it is best for such a stuffinge
which comes with aheat & cold there upon

An openinge oxymel cut phleme in the stomack
Take on Cychory roote 3 Parsley roots one or 2 fennell roots,
one borrage roote; one roote of briscus or buchers broome one
handfull of maiden heare one roote of asparagus, a handfull
of cloate leaves halfe a handfull Hissop, pith ye roots & boyle
all the ingredients in 3 pints of runninge water till allmost
halfe bee wasted, then streine it and put to it halfe a pinte
of Einglish hony; boyle it to A pint then put to it as much
vinegar as will make it sharp scum it till it bee cleere
Take of it 2 or 3 spoon fulls at a time, and take it often

recipes.raw_title: & one pound of Sheeps suet shred verie small & boyle all
recipes.raw_body:
these together in a potle of the grounds of the strongest ale
you can gett, until it bee halfe boyley away then thicken it with
wheat flower untill it com to bee a spreadings Pulltis & lay
this hott upon the plague sore, or swellinge & this will hasten ye
breakinge of it; sooner then the plaister aforesaid, & after it
is broken the plaister will heale it, beinge only layd upon it
all though these bee one two or three holes deepe in the flesh
as Experience hath Showed in ye lower groine, without any
tents put into the holes; only take the plaister of everie
12 houres & wipe it & lay it on againe & when one side is
worne to the cloth you may change ye other side
Peter White
A Prowringe  Ale to bee takne 28 dayes together betweene
the begininge of March & ye End of May & 20 days at ye fall of
ye leafe
Take 3 gallons of Stronge Ale well boyled for feare of Sowringe
fenna 6 ounces; kernells of Ashen keyes 2 ounces Barberies husked
2 ℥ roots of Pollippdin of the oke 5 ℥, fennell seeds i℥ & halfe
anniseeds i℥ of the roots of the wood Sassafras i℥, slicd End one
of these that are to bee sliced, & beate them into grosse
powder & if you will have it verie stronge; bruise the sena
verie small, put all these into A thin Canvas bagg & put in in
to the ale when it hath done workinge & after 48 houres you
may drinke thereof, halfe A pinte in the morninge &
som what lesse at night goinge to bed more or lesse as you
find it to worke
for faintinge & swooninge it may bee giveen to
child-bed women
Take the blew bottles which grow in Corne distill them &
give them the water to drinke warme, som will put
thereto a litle treackle
for A consumption
Take a reare Egge, as much powder of amber as will cost 2 pe
nie, stire it up & letit bee your breakefast

recipes.raw_title: Atiffirny, take allso the coursest gray salt, & after
recipes.raw_body:
you have dryed it by the fire, beat & searse it; than take of
Each powder alike quantity & put them into skillet, puttinge
unto them as much white wine vinigar; as will make the pow
der like picldell; adinge also as much sallet oyle as there was
Vinegar, then set it over the fire; & boyle it till a quart bee boyled
in, stirringe it all the time of the boyleinge; then take it of
the fire & keepe it stiringe till it bee cold, & it will bee a pfect
Ointm; you must anoynt the place morninge & eveninge (
it will smart verie much, & when the roughnesse is off; if pimples
of red flesh arise; touch them with a litle Algyptiacum & yt
will take them doune
A seare Cloth
Take i7 ounces & halfe of the best salet oyle you can geet,
& 5 ounces of castle-demor-soape, & one ounce of barrowes grease
& boyle all thsses together in a new Earthen pan, a prity.
while after they bee melted, then take 8 ounces of ceruse &
4 ounces of mingard (which is white, & reed lead), both searsed
fine to powder, & mingle them, & put them into the pan and
keepe them continualy boylinge & stiringe with a bedstaffe or
such like: untill the coller of it doth begin to change browne
then take it of the fire; & put in to it halfe an ounce of
oyle of bayes, then take halfe A yard of new 3 qter Cloth
& dip it into it till the salve bee thicke; on both sides of the
remainder you may put into any small pan; for to make
plaisters for any greene wound or swellinge, & it cures it will
by gods asistance cure it without any scarre, This searecloth
beinge applid to any plague, sore or swelinge, with gods
asistance Either dissolve the swellinge & drain it by moisture
upon the salve, which must bee taken of Everie 12 houres
& Clensed & then laid on againe, otherwise it will breake
it; I have had the Experience of it upon myselfe for a
plague sore; & upon divers others for swellings
Likewise for the spidier breakinge of the a plague sore
gather of Red sage & Rue, of smalidge & fetherfew of Each
of these a good handfull & shred or pound them together





For the Cough or stuffinge
Take A quart of runinge water A Pinte of vir iuyce one great fenell
roote 6 parseley Roots 2 or 3 licorise roots too good spoonfull of annised
halfe a hand full of Rosemary, as much hysop boyle all these till
halfe bee consumed, then streine it out & put to it 6 ounces of sugar
& neere a qter of a pint of vinigar; boyle it till it bee of the ordinary
thicknesse of syrup, & let it bee taken 3 or 4 spoonfulls at a time,
oft times in A day, Especially first & last, this seldom faiyles.

Syrup of Eldern
Take Eldere berries Picke them from the stalkes, & put as many
of them as will fill it, into a skillet, set it on the fire & keepe it
continualy stirringe; till the iuce bee comms from them; then
take that iuyce & straine it & boyle it againe till the iuyce
bee halfe consumed then take it of and weigh it & put to it a
pinte of iuyce 3 qters of sugar; boyle the sugar with it till it
bee about the thicknesse of a conserve; & use to take 3 spoone
fulls of it fastinge

For the scurvey in the mouth
Take A little Hony put into it A little mithridate; a little pwder of
burnt Alom boyle it A little upon the fire; till it grow thickish
then put in A drop of vineger or 2 or 3; & anoynt your gumes & teethe
with it.

For a Could or cough of the Lungs
Licorice 3 ounces, Rhubarb, 1 dram pennidies 2 ounces, Oris rootes
halfe an ounce of oyle of anniseeds 3 drames, gum dragon one
dram; Red rose water one penniworth, hard sugar one qter of
a pound; steepe the gum dragon 12 houres in the Red rose water
which don put all the ingredients into A mortar & beate them
to a past; of which make litle cakes & keepe them close in A
box, usinge them morninge, Eveninge & at othertimes as
need Requires

For A scald head
Take thick oystershells new & cleere & make them verie cleane
then dry them by the fire, & beate & searce them through






Take spanish salt & burn it, with A hot iron till you may
make it into fine powder, beinge in powder take so many yolks
of eggs as will make the salt a salve, & mixe it well together
and apply it, after twice dresinge, you may lay on your heallinge
salve
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A salve to lay to a cut presently
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
whit salt fine beaten,the whit of an Egge, a quantity of rose
water, mix them well together, wet two in it & lay to the cut: 24:
houres, wash the wound with the parties owne water; then dresse
is as before; & lay a plaister ov it if the wound grow ae it up
with dead flesh then correct it with bornt allum; & with the
powder of pcipitate which is red
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
An Exellent Pultis for breast or faice to take
out the Ague
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Take A good  A good peice of deeres suet, melt it & put 2 yolks
of Eggs well beaten stirit continually; put in a spoonfull of
English hony, as much whit bread greated as will make it thick
spread it upon a cloth & lay it to hot
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
for A fistula
Ritinoli albi, Et aluminis opt ana 4: Lapis Caliminaris:
dimid unta fiat pulvis subtilis:
Put These in A Pan & Burne them as you doe allum, untill
it bee perfectly dry then beat it into fine powder, & when
you use it take faire runninge water, boyle it a litle, then take
it from the fire, & put in the powder by degrees as long as it
shewes any simperinge, & reserve the faire & cleare water for
your use, castinge away the dreggs, if you will make it coole
put in a dram Camphire, with the other powder before the
burninge if you would hqve it more dryinge put in halfe
a dram of terra Lemnis
Let the water be A quart of runninge water, & a qter of a
a pint of plaintaine water.

recipes.raw_title: To make the Chiefe of all Plaisters & Salves
recipes.raw_body:
Take halfe A Pound of Rozin, as much pecosen, a quarter of a pound of franck-
incense; as much virgins wax, mastick one ounce A quarter of a pound of
deeres suet; 2 drames of Camphire, a quarter of a pound of Venice turpentine
melt the one & beat the other to fine powder; then searce them; then
lett it boyle upon a soft fire; by a little & a little, strew in your powder
& keepe it with a Continuall stirringe, your gumes beinge in & dissol.
ved, Put in your turpentine with som myirth that beinge dissolved
take it of the fire & streane it through a linnien cloth in t a pottle
of whit wine; then let it stand till it be could; then worke it up
into balles; & let it lie in the wine, & it will bee like Alliblaster

It will keepe 7 yeares good especially for greene wounds &
ackes; it will suffer noe dead flesh to grow

To stop bleedinge in any cut

Dry vine leaves beate them to powder; & stop the wound there
with; / or this / Take Bole almonick & beate it to
Powder & apply it to the wound

The greene ointment

Take of may butter unsalted; 12 pound of boares grease 8 pound
of Rosin 2 pound of frankincense one pound of sallet oyle, 4
Pints o vierdigrease 20 ounces, greene tobacco as much as yo can
Clasp in both hands, lavender cotten lavender, Parsley, comfrey
sorrell Elldern; tyme; maciacom, Red sage, Red mints, set well;
selfe heale, yellow masse that growes on ockes, osmon, Adders
tongue or pine, hysop, Costmary of Each of all these A handfull
Chop them small put them into A pot with a pound of deeres suet
& as much bees waxe; cover it close, & put it into horse mucke
2 or 3 dayes foot deepe; there let it stand a month then take
it out & boyle it an houre; then take it of againe & streane it
into a pot & put fresh herbs into it & sett it 20 dayes more in
to mucke then take it out and boyle it againe, & when you
take it of put in som oyle of spicke & stir it & straine
tis best at 7 yeares ould

To kill a fellon & cure it

recipes.raw_title: and halfe so much copporas beinge whit straine it
recipes.raw_body:
and keepe it close stopt in a glasse; it is best maid in may
for then theire hearbs are in theire prime
for the prickinge of a thorne a whit=loorfe
boyle wheat flower & whitwine till it bee thicke; spread it
upon a cloth & lay it to as hot as can bee indured
or this
Take a little black sope; English hony han & put wheat flower
well mixed together, spread it together upon a cloth & lay it to
To make a Balme good for any wound
Take aquavita, venice turpentine oyle of roses; of Each a
pint boyled softly; put in h An ounce of verdigrease maid into
fine powder; then boyle it to a pfect substance & use it
To make an oyntmt for a burninge with gunpowder
or scaldings with water
Take a quart of bores grease; grain salt two handfulls, house
leeck 3 heads; stamp them together, & put it to new sheeps dung
goose dunge of Each 2 handfull; stamp them well together
without the grease, that done mix the grease with them
& fry them upon a soft fire; then straine it & keepe it
for your use
to breake an impostume
Take a whit lilly rootse2 onions boyle them in water untill
they bee soft; stamp them fry them, in swines grease, spread it
upon a cloth thicke; lay it to the sore as hot as may bee
indured, renewinge it everie 24 houres till if breaks
or This
Take wormwood, mallowes & mugwort of Each a handfull
stamp them & mingle them with a qter of a pound of
swines grease; fry them & put them ^ put in an handfull of
wheat bran 4 ounces of hony, boyle them till thy bee
thicke; spread it upon a cloth & lay it to as hot
as you can Abide

recipes.raw_title: To take a fire out of burninge and to
recipes.raw_body:
heale the same

take hoggs dunge and the whitest of hens dunge, boyle them together
till they loocke verie yellow, streane them out into pot, when
it is could amoynt the place; wet lawne (such as hath noe starch
in it & lay upon it; keepe it with wett clothes and anointinge till
the fire bee out & apply this followinge, Take the yellow
mosse that grows upon the brick walls, Picke it verie cleand chop
motton just verie small; put them into a posnet seeth them till
they look yellow if it boyle too fast it will loocke black, streine
it through a cloth amoynt ye burninge there with but allwis
mellt it before you use it

A most approved medicn for the Plague

Take 3 pints of Muscadins; Rue sage, of Each a hand full;
boyle them well upon a charcole fire till one pint bee consumed
then streine them till all the juce bee out of the herbs set it
on the fire againe; put into it longe peper; ginger nutmegge
beaten to powder; of each one ounce; boyle all together a litle
more; take it of the fire; put in one ounce of mithradate 2
ounces of treackle a qter of a pint of angelica water or
aquavita, and use as followeth; If any thinks themselves infec
take morninge and Evening one spoonful hot or could, &
sweat after it; if not infected, in the heat of the plague
take not above halfe a spoonfull at a time & not above
3 times a weecke next under good trust to this

To cure A canker in the mouth or a sore mouth

Take a gallon of runinge watter hissop; violet, strawberie
planton Endife sorrell; rue succory, bayes, an handfull of
the leaves of each; seeth all those till halfe bee consumed
then streine it, put in a pint of whit wine seeth then but a litle
or not at all so that it stand upon the fire; then put in as
much Einglish hony as will make it sweet, scum it cleane, take
it of the fire, and put in allom to the bignesse of a walnut

recipes.raw_title: roots, crocodilium or cartima roots; balelion roots Celidine
recipes.raw_body:
roots of each 2 ounces; if the roots bee greene you must beat them
If dry stamp them to powder, mak one ounce; seeds of the feder
take one ounce; red wax 2 ounces fine treackle 2 ounces; 3 ounces
of rasberries through ripe. ℥ ounces of aquavita; one ounce of
sinamone, halfe an ounce of ligued aloes; let all these bee well
stamped & put into the glasse or pot to ye other; stop it verie close
then make a fire under the caldren that the water bee hot
without boylinge keepe it soe for 2 or 3 dayes the longer ye better
if the fire goe out in the night; make it againe & you must keepe
it on the fire the longer; then take the vessell of  & sett it in the
sun all the sumer after; keepe it all the while verie clos covered
or stoped the oulder the oyle is the better it is, it is verie good to put
Everie yeare som of that hearb juce of that hearb st. Johns wort
the blossoms & the seeds well stamped; beinge sodden some 5 or 6
houres in oyle olive then put them into a cloth & streane them verie
hard Cast away the hearbs & flowers with the blossoms & put
that new oyle into your ould oyle if you cannot gett them in ye
aforesaid season you may take them at any other times
The virtues pf this oyle are infinit; yu will name the it hath
as much virtue as the true & rich balme; it is good for all maner
of gold greifes; as well within as without the body, for yesciatica
the cole gout in rubing the place with it, for the quartern or
tertian ague; with anoynting the vains of the back an hour be
for it cometh; it cureth Collicam pallienem when they anoynt
the brest or stomick with it or put a little of it into a glister, or if
a woman hath her fruit dead in her wombe lett her take 3 or 4
drames & shee shall bee delivered incontnently; it is verie good for all
sores of brests & stomacke; above all other things it is Exelent
for the Plague; anoyntinge the veins of the backe & drinkinge
2 drams & a halfe in whitwine, but that  must not bee
drunke; before ye sixt hour after the sicknesse is begun; & to
rub the place of the sickness is also good; for any ould or
new wound; Esspecially for any bruise; if you drinke
a litle of it use2 or 3 mornings together-





To make the oyle of Saint Johns Wort

Gather in may or June ye hearb Caled St Johns wort before it
begins to florrish or have flowres Stamp it in a cleane mortar, put
it in to A glasse; power to it as much Whit wine as will cover it
all over; ad to it Sallet oyle ye hight of 2 fingers & stop it up
verie Close; upon sant Johns day in ye morninge after sun up,
gather of the sayd hearbeblossoms; laying the blossoms by till untill
you have stamped the hearb & the stalkes; then take them out
and Put in the flowers, & bruise them a litle; your flowers or blosoms
must wigh 4 times as much as your herbs that you mingled first
then mingle all together in som glasse or earthen pot, then put
in more wine & oyle (as before) set it in the sun (well stoped) foure
12 or 15 dayes; after when the seeds of St Johns Wort shall bee
ripe; gather in the morninge after the sun is up, Stampe them well
& mingle them with ye herbe & blossoms; you might put noe wine
in then only oyle ye seeds must bee the 3d or 4th part in weight
to the hearb before the wine or oyle was put into it; the oyle must
bee in all to the quantity of an hand full or 2; after this set
a Calderen of watter on the fire with hay & straw in the botom
Put in your said glasse or Pott not Stoped; make the water to
seeth 3 or 4 houres till the wine or most part bee consumed,
you shall know in this manner; take A litle of the Substance
upon a Sticke end; cast it into the fire; if it burne with out
any noyse; it is a signe there is noe wine lefft
If the Substance bee aboue 5 or 6 pound you shall put to these
things followinge; accordinge to ye weight or measure wee
Shall shew you; and keepe allwais a good p[ro]portion accordinge
to the weight of the substance Which shall bee more or lesse
then 5 pound; Take brimstone halfe a pound of comon
Whit sallt 8 ounces of Earth wormes a dish full well washed
in water; honey rosat or other hony if it bee sodden & scumed
10 ounces of venice turpentine well washed in faire water
Lard of hogg well Stamped; the iuce of tuxus barbatus
the Juce of Whit or blacke dictamnur of Each 4 ounces
safron 3 ounces Putama roots, cartion roots; Imperatoria





For Women 24
Take the husks of Almonds dryed to powder; & give to drin
ke in plantaine water blood warme; they must bee the husks of Jur
den Almonds pared of with akniffe

Or this
Take 3 grains of muske; wrap them up in a linnen cloth, and bind
them to your navell till they stay

For A scouringe or fluxe proved
Take A peice of fresh beefe heate it on A knives poynt; Scrape
with Chalke upon it verie thicke; & lay it to the navell, lay on
a fresh peice every day untill it stay

A salve for A wrench or sore
Take Rosin; Posin; of Each a pounde wax & Franckincense of
Each A qter of A pound; when they are almost moulten; put to
A qter of a pound of wethers suet; boyle them together halfe
a qter of an houre softly; Streine them together with A ppotle
of whit wine; boyle them all to gether till the wine bee som thinge
wasted; put to it an ounce of masticke finely beaten; & lett
it boyle a little, take it of the fire; when it is almost could;
put it to 2 drames of Camphire beaten to powder; a qter of a
pound of turpentine; stirringe it till it bee cold oyle your
hands; & make it up in to roules & keepe it

For the swellinge of Chillderens Cods
Take Red wine; red rose flowres bruise them a litle
beate them to gether halfe an houre; Dip a linnen cloth
in it & lay to the place as hott as may be
indured

recipes.raw_title: A medicin for the swellinge or inpostum
recipes.raw_body:
in the face
Take seage leaves shred verie small put sallet oyle & mace
to it boyle them together till the strengcg bee out of the sage
& mace, make a twillt of White Wool as bigge as the place
greeced, Wet it in the oyle and apply it warm, Ever as it
drieth wet the Wool againe weare it day & night if it bee
taken in time it will keep it from breakinge, however it will
speedily breake it.
A verie good oyntmt for all mane of ackes
Take A quart of neats foote oyle of suthernwood; of wormwood
of bay leaves of Each an handfull stamp them well together
and put there to the gall of an oxe as much sallet oyle
as gall; fry them all togther streine them; & put them
into A glass & anoynt the place greeved; being well
Rubed in with A warme hand
For scaldinge
Take tenn Eggs Rosted as hard as may bee; take only the whits
verie small; halfe A pound of unsallted butter; fry them together
and when it loketh black streane it & anoynt the place greved
& lay a fine Cambrick cloth over it; for laune will cleave Every
dressinge you must take of the of the old & make the sore Cleane
To make Asear cloth good for all ackes; bruse,
sores & streanes
Take A pint of sallet oyle set it on a sofft fire; when it be
gins to boyle put to it halfe Apound of red leade (a pound will
make it too thicke; let it be firmly beaten; stirrit yt it may
not Clodder; when it is sodden thicke that it will rowle; put to
it as much Rosin, finly beaten; as the bignesse of A henns
Egge then dip your Cloth init  Approved





A gargell to rayes flegme 22

Make A Posset of millke preivinge most berger streine it
streane it through ACloth sweetne it with sugar gargle
with it when you please; & if you lett any goe downe in to
your stomick it doth much good for it scowreth the stomack
Aproved

To provoke sleepe Aproved

Take oyle of roses & rose water & womans milke temper them
all together & anoynt the temples of the head

for sore breasts

Take of Rozin beaten to fine powder 6 ounces of: vergins wax
4 ounces of turpentine one ounce o English hony 2 spoonfull
of sheeps suet 2 ounces; melt all these to gether & make A sear
cloth & apply it

An approved ointment for any greene wound what ever

Take 6 ounces of gumme Cemny, 6 ounes of venice Turpentine 4
ounces of Rames suet clarifide 4 ounces of hoggs grease clarifid
make your gumm verie small then mellt all to gether upon a smal
fire; when they bee throughly melted; streine them through
a fine cloth in to a pot; you may apply it either with tent
or plaister

An Exelent salve for ould or new sores

Take A quart of sallat oyle 5 ounces of red lead 2 ounces cel
cuse; whit lead 5 ounces; wax halfe a pound Rozen halfe a
pound duckes grease one ounce; dogs grease one ounce goose
grease one ounce; boyle all these toll they bee blacke &
com to bee stiff; then put into 2 ounces o Laydantiam
A dram of gumfry grond verie small together in the coolinge
make it up in balles with ducks grease for that is the best

against any ache

Take an ounce of coriander seed one ounce of fenigreeke, beat
them small boyle them in a squart of muscadine till
it comes to A pint streane it & aply it t the
greaved warme





An Oyntment for ye Hemerds |21

Take 2 ounces of bees waxe halfe an ounce of litargie of gouls ground
verie fine falfe an ounce of mirrhe; one ounce of masticke verie fine
halfe A pound of fresh hoggs suett; mellt the suet & the wax to
gether; then worke all together; the powders are all to bee finly seard prband

for stayinge stayinge ye bleedinge of ye Hemerods

Make cleere posset drinke A quart 2 handfull of yarrow pickt verie
cleane & washt; put in the yarrow & boyle it untill it comes to a pinte
& halfe; after the boylinge take out the yarrow & clense it put in
one qter of a pound of sugar; & soe drinke a qter of a pint in
the morninge fastinge; as much when you goe to bed

or this
brusie yarrow & anoynt the place greeved with the iuce of it

To breake the hemerodes
All the foresaid ingredients in the oyntmt exept the Hoggs suet
and but one ounce of waxe grond upon a stone with linseed oyle

The plaister for the backe
Colliffolli halfe a pound; Rozen a qter of a pound salet oyle
one pint & a qter; bees wax one qter of A pound ; of gumme
Elemny 3 ounces; hony a qter of A pound Red lead halfe a pound
Litergy of gouls one q of A pound these two last finly beaten
& seaced; boyle these on a moderate fire till you see it change
the collar by dropinge a drop upon the board; you findinge it
to grow hard; ad thereto one ounce of masticke camphir
one ounce C dissolve ye Camphier with oyle; mirrh one ounce
of Ceruse 4 ounces finely beaten & searced prband

for A sore head oft approved
Take A handfull of time as much Rosemary halfe as
much sage Chop them & seeth them in prish butter
or hogs grease, steere them well then streane them
and mix with them a penniworth o staues aloe
finly beaten

recipes.raw_title: A good handfful wash & chop them small, & seeth them with
recipes.raw_body:
water & oatemeale; when it is boyled put in a little grosse
pepper & butter; & the pith of mutton, & soe eat it as you finde
cause

An exelent salve for burninge

Take bees waxe deeres suet; & may butter of each a like quantity
Put them into a skillet & mingle them over the fire then measure
it in a porringer, & take just quantity of salbet oyle; then ming
le them well together; heat a silver basson over the fire & put
them into it, with a porringer & a halfe of snowewater, or more
as the quantity is make them heat together 2 or 3 houres untill it
looks whit; This is exeedinge good for any skaldinge or
burninge by fire or gunpowder, if any sore bee inflamed, or any
heate whatever; blastinge or venome; it is to bee used could sprad upon
cloth or with a fither upon the sore

Another medicin for the wombe

Take the whit of 2 eggs 2 spoonfull of redrose water beate them
to gether verie well then take of the froth & put in alitle nutmegge
& sugar & take it 3 or 4 mornings fastinge

A Cataplasme for ye Hemerodes
Take of mellilot mallowes of each a handfull; boyle them in
millke untill they bee sofft then beate them to to peeces in a morter
& put them in againe to the Millke; & Ad unto them an ounce of
the brann of linseed & An ounce of the brann of fennigreeke &
3 ounces of the oyle of elderne; & make it a pulltisse, but when it
is allmost could ad unto it 2 yolks of eggs beaten & a litle safron
Dr. Smith

An Exelent Pulltis for a sore brest
Take creame & Red sage & merneht crumes, & boyle them together
untill it bee thicke when you take it of the fire put
into it linseede oyle & apply hit hot to the brest
but first bath it well with strong beere

recipes.raw_title: for a sore of any kinde new or ould Esplly for
recipes.raw_body:
sore leggs

Take A pint of Civitt oyle 10 ounces of red lead, 2 ounces of bees
waxe; beate your lead verie fine; & slice your waxe verie thin boyle
your oyle & waxe a qrter of an hour in a skillet then take it of
the fire ; & put in your lead by litle & litle, Keepinge it contin-
ually stirringe & let it boyle untill it looke blacke; then dry it upon
a fire pan as you did the other; when it is boyled then dip your clothe
as fast as may bee take heed of over boylinge it; if it bee too stiff
Put in a litle more oyle; keepe it from fire or sun it lasts not
above A yeare

for the yellow jaundice

Make a quart of Psset Ale verie cleere put into it 3 or 4 dock roots
the roots must bee cut that the pith may be taken out, then
then let them boyle in the Ale till it com to a pint; then take it
of & put as much saffron in it as will make it yellow, & let the
patient drinke a draught of it morninge & eveninge when
hee goes to bed & once in the afternoone the oftner it is takne ye
sooner it healeth

Against miscaringe

Take halfe a pint of red cowes milke & 2 or 3 spoonfull of red
rose water, & a branch of rosemary set it to the fire till it boyle
up; then take it of & sweeten it with sugarcandy & let he drinke
an indiffrent draught fastinge

for the same

Take red cowes millk & put to it a litle red sage & boyle them
together & sweeten it to your tast; & drinke of it fastinge

Another Exellent

Take the Treads of new layd eggs & a litle purple silke
Chopt small mingle them with a litle sugar take it
often but Esspecially when you feele yourselfe ill

An Exelent medicin for the wombe

Take knot greasse & broad Plantain roots of each a good

 of Canary sacke into an Earthen vessell & melt it then take it of the fire & take halfe a pound of venice turpentine washt in red rose water & a pint & a halfe of sllet oyle power them into the pot that sacke & wax is in & then boyle them together untill they bee incorporated, then take them of the fire & Coole them thoroly, untill it bee could then take of the Cake & melt it againe; & put into it one ounce of sanders; stiringe continualy till it bee could; have care as the sanders bee verie good; you may in the melting ad to it naturall ballsom, halfe an ounce of sanguis draconis one ounce, & you must ad a litle ambergreene; The virtue of this bal sum It is for wounds, ackes, bruses inward or outward, ye Collick burnings scaldings; Kings Evil, women in labour plurisies; broken veines, the quantity is the bignesse of an halfe nut; in posset ale white wine or sack outward apply it verie hott; it is allso good  for sore brests

An approved good seare cloth for  streins ackes bruises, pricks with A thorne any botch or boyle or for stoping of drawinge or strengthininge. Take A pound of oyle olive the best, halfe halfe a pound of red lead a qter of whit lead, the rare receipt thus ordered; one qter of  red lead halfe a pound of whit, a qter of castle sope, beat your lead verie fine & slice your sope verie thin, put them into a deep well leaded pipkin; & set it upon a sofft charcole fire Continually stiring it till the red collar turns gray, drop a drop of it upon a could fire pann & it comes clere from the  pan it is boyle if not boyle it untill it will then put in an ounce of the oyle of bayes; & as much as 2 walnuts of boares grace & soe let it boyle a qter of an hur; then  Either spread it upon clothes or make it up in roles keepe it from drye & it will bee good 7 yeares





for the cough approved 117

Take a qrter of Runninge water & as much of hysop & colts
foot water put in to it a pound of raysins of ye sun 9 or 10 figgs
one good sponfull of Anniseeds & 2 sticks of licorise scraped
& sliced; let both ye Anniseeds & that bee bruised in a morter;
then set all these upon the fire & let them boyle till the liquor
be consumed to A quart then streane it & put in to it as much
candis as will make it verie sweete & soe keepe it & drinke
as often as you please; Mrs Webb

To Cut flegme

Take A good quantity of parsley & fenel roots the piths
taken out & seeth them in an Earthen pott with water; with
A good quantity of wine vinegar whit and red, & let it boyle
A good while; then lett run through a boulter; then caste
the roots away; & put in to it A good quantity of sugar;
boyle it to a thin sirrop & take a spoonfull or 2 at a time
A Webb

for wind & paine in the stomack

Take one ounce of carraway seeds & as much many Fenn
ell seeds 3 or 4 large lemon or orange pilles well dryed
one nutmeg finly grated A large stick of sinamond
make all these int a powder, & mix them with theire
weight of sawced sugar; keepe it close in A prper
& one hour before you eat take a spoonfull of it

for sore : filinge or in flamed Eyes

Take an Egg & rost it hard; then cut of the top & put in
as much whit coppor as as a nut & a litle whit rose water
put these in A cloth & squeece them as longe as any
water will come out of them of which take @ wash
your Eyes

recipes.raw_title: Take the yolks of 30 new laid Eggs a qrter of goots or
recipes.raw_body:
red cowes milke a pint of Red rose water halfe a pound of
dates; & a pint of snailes, a few cloves & an ounce of Sinimon
Steeped in lifemit water & an ounce of powder of amber
beate these to gether & put them into a still with a qucke
fire; take of this 3 or 4 times a day 3 or 4 spoonfulls at a time
in your broth wine or beeve

 A pretious water for sore Eyes

Take an Egg shell & fill it full with the juyce of house leeke
and put in as much whit Copper as as A great Pins heade
& sett it on the embers & let it disstill then scum it wiht a
feather & streane shell & all

Another

Take trefoyle & streane it & put damaske rose water to it
& drop it into youre Eye

An admirable water for wind ye stone & megrim
from ovinge of the hart & fumes from the mother

Take a quart of whit wine & a pint of Sacke, & steepe it in as
much broad time as it will well wet, put to it an ounce gallin
gall, as much aromaticus gall banus of cloves, mace ginger &
grains of Each A qrter of an ounce all in powder; steep these all
night, put them in the morninge, into a comon still, and follow
it with asofft fire, ye quantity isto bee taken is 3 spoonefulls
at a tyme





A fistula water 115

Sett faire runninge watter upon Asoft fire when it begins a litle
to simper strew into it beaten Allum & whit coppor as finley beaten
& searsed; if you will have it verie stronge; then burne your
copporace; of Each a like quantity, never leave strewinge intill
it leave simperinge for then it is anough; then take it of the
fire & keepe it in a glasse

A water to Abate Proud flesh or cleanse corupt sore

Take a handfull of sage washed cleane A quart of ale or beere
a peece of Allum about the bignesse of A walllnut seeth them all
together till halfe bee wasted beinge warme wash the sore

A water pinpall for all wounds & cankers

Take Red Sage leaves Salindine woobine leaves of Each an
handfull; seeth them in A gallon of springe water till halfe
bee wasted; put in a pynt of Einglish hony set it on the fire
againe; & put in allum & whit copporace finly beaten of
Each an ounce; A penniworth of grains briused let them seeth
4 or 5 wallops & scum it with a feither then let it stand till it
bee could; the thinest keepe for thy selfe & use for greene
wounds & Sores; the thick for ould sores, & when you dresse
the sores lay a vine leafe or the selme of a motton or beale
upon it

A receipt for a mouth water or a canker

Take a gallon of runinge water; wild woodbind leaves,
bramble leaves Seage of Each 2 good hand full Single colu
mbines; of Each A handfull; hisope sallendine of Each a
qrter of A handfull; Boyle all these in water till a qrter
bee consumed, then streane it out & put thereto a pint
of Eanglish Hony; & an ounce of rock allum; boyle it
againe a qrter of an houre & skiminge it & so keepe it
for your use

An Admirable water for a consumption

recipes.raw_title: A water for A canker & to wash A greene wound
recipes.raw_body:
Take a hand full of woodbind leaves A handfuull of Red Branble
leaves, A handfull of sorrell; & boyle a pennieroyall of salentine
of rosemary; of Each A handfull of red sage; of hearb grace
of red fennell an a halfe handfull; Boyle all these in a gallon
of runinge water; untill the hearbs bee soft then put to a spoon
full & a halfe of hony halfe a hand full of graine & peice
of allom; boyle them a little stopped & it will keepe a yeare
when you use it let it bee warmed

for verie sore watery red Eyes

Take ould whit rose water a qrter of a pint & put into it
as much stone sugar in powder as a great haselenut; & to this
put 5 or 6 slices of cleane crapt licorice; lett all these stand
one night & in the morninge power softly the clearest of this
water in to cleane glasse & wash the Eyes often with this
with a fither

to cleare thick Eyes

Put whit sugar candy in to A bladder & hange it over warme
water untill it bee melted; & drop it into the Eye with a
fether.

for red sore Eyes

Take wormwood & stamp it & beate the whit of an Egge &
put to it with a little whit rose water streane them togather
then put som of it betweene 2 clothes & the could beinge
taken of lay it to your Eyes

A water for ye Eyes

It is maid by putinge a dram of vitrum antimony in
pallpable pouder into a pint of whit rose water (if you
can have it) or Else take other; & so lett it stand close stoped
in a warme place steringe the glass 3 or 4 times in a day, then
after three or 4 dayes use it but let it not bee sterred
but wvrie cleare setled, when you power it out againe
if you find it two sharp sharpe allay it with a little
posterne water )

recipes.raw_title: An Exelent water for any sore or to take out the ague
recipes.raw_body:
Rt A pound of lavinder a pound of Rosemarie; a pound of sage, a
pound of honnisuckle leaves; a pound of bramble leaves & a pound
of elderne budds a qrter of or pint of honie and a qrter of a pound
of allom; the herbes must bee shredd &; boyled in a pottle or 3
quarts of water; accordinge as you see convenience boyle it the
halfe away keepinge it stirrd all the while; boyle it in an iron
Pott; or in an earthen pipkin, streane out the dcoction;
then put in the Hony & allom stirringe it till all bee incor
porated then put it in to bottles for your use; this hath cured
a sore breest that hath had holes in it; only by washing it verie
hott & dippinge raggs in the water & tentinge the holes, it is
to bee maid in May:

Morlint holy water

wall flowers cowslipps; Rosemary buglasse, mariegoulds
pinks, damask roses, clovegillis flowers; be finly pickt & a pinte
of Each of them infused in sacke ad to them an handfull of
Balme a groats worth of saffron; as much large mace two nut
meggs; one peniworth of currancs; & coliander seeds of each
still these in a rose still close pasted; & put into your veca
ber whit sugar candy beaten small; som beatte gould; let
the glasses stand in warme water; you may save the first
runinge by it selfe; that will bee stronge ye next will bee
good the last but weake

A cock water good for A Consumption & cough of ye lungs

Take an ould Red Cocke well dressed; leave his stones with
in him; one ounce of China roots sliced thin, 2 ounces of ju
iubes halfe a pound of rasins of the sonn stoned & 2 good
handfulls of coultsfoot, boyle all these in a gallon of
runinge watter but first lett the cocke bee well bruised
bones & all, & put into the watter; boyle these upon a soft
fire; untill it comes to a pottle; & then put them all into
a still & distill them; & give it to the partie 2 or 3 times
a day warmed with a little sugar)





A disstilled watter for the stone

Take 2 handfull of saxafrage of wild time of pelitorie of
the wall; parsley of each alike 3 or 4 radish roots, briuse
the herbs a little & slicethe rootes in thin slices, then lay all
in steepe together in a gallon of new milke & so disstill
it out with a soft fire & keepe it in a glass for your use
this water is to bee maid Either in the latter End of may or in the
begininge of  June; because hearbs then bee in theire chifest
strength; It is to bee taken one in 3 or 4 weecks for 3 mor
nings together fastinge six spoonfull of the water, & as much
of whit wine put together & a peece of nutmege sliced
and put into it, & the quantity of A hasellnut of fine whit
sugar; beinge all warmed a little at the first & soe drink it
up & eate the slices of nutmeg; After it Either walke or ride
or use som Exercise

An Exellent stomick water & to prevent sicknesse
and good against the spleene

Take greene wallnuts & when you can cut them shell and all
distill them & use them as you have occation; a few cloves
with them will doe well; distill this water about the
23th of July

An Exelent water Catholcon for all inward diseases

Take hoggs lunge & distill it; give the partie greeved 2 or 3
spoonfulls of this water sweetned with sugar; to give it a
good relish; you must take the materiall in may; when
the hoggs have gon abroad & have Eaten all sorts of hearbs
then is the time to distill it; if the sicknesse have not beene
unto death it hath wrought admirable cures for inward
diseases; as hath beene often proved by A gentlewoman

An Exelent Sweet water

Rp a quart of the beest damaske rose water, put thereto
one graine of muske; one graine civet & one of amber:greece
shacke these together & it is maid

wind & stone
Take Mallowes Camomil & pelitory of Each one handfull
Anniseeds & fenell seeds; bruise of Each one spoonfull A qrter
of an ounce of Electuanu lenitiuinu; when you have maid the
decoction of the hearbs & seeds; streane it and dissolue therein your
lectuary; and when you haue pured it into the blader light a
Pipe of tobacco & blow in the fume there of keepeinge it in
with your hands; & administer it blood warme use it once in
2 dayes till the grife bee removed

The Lady Richardsons water for the winde & pssion
of the hart & the stone Aproved
Take A Pint of Sacke & a qrte of white wine & steepe in them
as much broad time; as they will wett, Steep allso one ounce of
gallingall beaten one ounce of gallinus calamus supra Aromat
& of Cloves mase ginger grains of Each A qrter of an ounce, all in
powder these steeped together all night; still them in an ordinary
still with a sofft fire; & drinke thereof 3 sponefulls at a time
with A litle sugar

Mrs Hobbarts rare water for weake & distemp childr
Take Halffe Apeck of snayles ppared (as is derected) put them
in A comon still with Coults foot water; pimpnell water A
grimonie; scabious & Hisop water of Each a pint of Succory
water halfe A pint A pound of rasins stoned & sliced; one ounce
of Licorise scraped & sliced; as much anniseeds bruised, these
still with a softt fire; when you give it lett the pporcon
bee 4 spoonfulls warmed & sweetned with sugarcandy
in the morninge fastinge & at 4 of the clock in the afternoone
the snayles are ppared thus, put them into a bowle
or pale with a good quantity of sage; let them lye cover
ed with it all night; then picke them from it into warme
water A bassin; & straw salt Amonge them & stir them
to gether to make them sicke & spitt then put them into
warme water to comfort them where they will purge
them sl shifftinge them into 3 warme waters by which time
they will bee dead; & loock cleare & wholsomly then take
them out and dry them and put them into the still shells &
all

recipes.raw_body:
Take of saxifrage pellitory of the wall; garden parsley; wild
tyme; of each a good handful 2 or 3 horseredish roots 2 spoon
full of sorrell seeds; briuse the seeds slice the roots & shred the
hearbs infuse all together one night in 2 qrts of new millke
then still it in a rose still; take 3 or 4 spoonfull of this water
with as much renish or whit wine; 3 dayes before the full & change
of the moone & 3 dayes after

for the stone
Take of the Roots of fillupendula slice them & boyle them in
possett drinke & drink of it morninge & eveninge

another Aproved
Boyle two good handfull of reed plantaine in A pottle of mid
linge Ale to a quart; take halfe A pint morninge & eveninge
with A Peece of honiye after Each draught to the quantatie
of A small walnut

Put 7 pints of springe watter in A pipkin & 4 ounces of harts
horne; boyle it halfe away then streane it through a gellie
bagg then put to it A pint of whit wine 4 ounces of lose sugar

ved first in the morninge & last at night to prevent the
stone use it at the Change & full of the moone

recipes.raw_body:

morninge, If the former recept drives them into the body this
drink will compleat the cure
